title: First draft
items: Baseline on IBAC’s pre-2026 constraints, the three watchdogs’ joint February ask for a transparent funding process, June’s political finance repair bill and record FOI volumes.

The Carroll government’s seven weeks: the royal commission, the Office of the Special Prosecutor, and the IBAC bill extending jurisdiction to contractors and to conduct below a criminal threshold — together with the late amendment excluding already-addressed construction matters.
Bill status recorded as passed the Assembly on 10 September and at second reading in the Council when checked; not law.
Coalition position recorded as specific on this scandal and silent on the machinery; the Greens’ platform as the most complete and uncosted; no One Nation integrity policy located.

title: First draft
items: Baseline from the 2026–27 budget’s fiscal strategy, the Auditor-General’s November 2025 report on the state’s finances, the AAP and ABC readings of the budget papers, and the credit ratings as published.

The accrual surplus set beside the four-year cash deficits; interest compared with the regional road maintenance gap; the Suburban Rail Loop fare charge and the savings claim the Auditor-General contradicted.
The Coalition’s 10-year plan against the list of uncosted commitments recorded across parts 6 to 8; Labor’s $10.8 billion claim recorded as showing no arithmetic.
The Parliamentary Budget Office’s regional-versus-metropolitan finding quoted in full, including the reversal when five major projects are excluded.

title: First draft
items: Baseline from the Auditor-General’s December 2025 transition report, AEMO’s 2026 electricity and gas outlooks, the 2026–27 default offer, the VRET progress report and the emissions inventory.

Labor’s SEC, zone and offshore-auction record, the gas rules as they stand, landholder payments and today’s pause of the Western Renewables Link (single wire story; to be updated when the Premier’s release appears); the Coalition’s gas, VNI West, firming, coal and buffer positions; the Greens’ standing policy and 2022 costing; One Nation’s Loy Yang launch.
Two comparison tables: keeping the lights on after 2028; bills, gas and farms.

title: First draft
items: Baseline from the September 2025 rental report, Anglicare’s 2026 snapshot, ABS completions against the 80,000-a-year target, the housing register and AIHW regional homelessness rates.

Labor’s delivered renter reforms, Big Housing Build and Regional Housing Fund counts, the May budget measures and the 2023 land-tax change; the Coalition’s stamp-duty, land-tax, short-stay and planning positions; the Greens’ rent cap and public-housing plan; One Nation’s housing page.
Party documents added as their own source type across the guide.

title: Housing comparison added
items: Part seven compares housing and cost-of-living positions; the plan for the remaining parts (energy, health, the budget, integrity going forward, the ballot, the final weighing) is listed on the series page.
